parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 algorithm, exact argparse behavior, .mjs ESM layout, no external dependencies, no node:crypto, and /output delivery requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It launched a workflow that assigned six implementation module groups to child agents, then planned a separate integration owner to read all libraries, write lib/index.mjs and /output/test2.mjs, and run end-to-end checks.
parallel.implementation: Five library areas completed through children and the parent eventually wrote lib/argparse.mjs itself after observing the argparse child had died and retried repeatedly.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration never ran to completion: the workflow remained killed with null result, one argparse child in progress, and the copied artifact lacked the expected test2.mjs entry point.
parallel.verification: Parallel performed substantial black-box probing and component-level checks, but the final integrated executable and required entry point were not verified because they were never assembled.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with an empty final response, no test2.mjs in the artifact, process_ok false, artifact_ok false, and 0 of 61 official samples passed.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same PBKDF2, argparse, ESM, local-module, no-dependency, and no-node:crypto obligations from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept ownership in a single trajectory, probing the executable, writing each library and the entry point, then iterating through differential failures without delegation.
serial.implementation: It produced test2.mjs plus sha1, hmac, pbkdf2, argparse, pytext, pyint, and pyexceptions modules, then fixed integer parsing, traceback, and output differences.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact contained the expected entry file and all library files, and the final response included the completed structure and entry-point code.
serial.verification: It ran documented sample cases, argument-surface tests, integer tests, randomized fuzzing, published SHA-1/HMAC/PBKDF2 vectors, and performance and hygiene checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite a complete artifact and extensive local checks, the official evaluator still marked the serial solution failed with 41 of 61 samples passed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome relation is both_fail because both completed evaluations mark solution_passed false. The attempts still differ materially: parallel timed out with no required test2.mjs and therefore 0/61 samples, while serial produced a complete artifact and passed 41/61 samples. The evidenced parallel contributor is the stalled argparse child and incomplete takeover that prevented final integration; the serial contributor is a single-owner lifecycle that wrote and verified the entry file before closure.
parallel_contributors: The argparse child was still in progress after three stall retries, while the workflow was killed with result null.
The parent recognized the stalled child and wrote argparse itself but did not complete the takeover into test2.mjs and final verification.
serial_contributors: Serial wrote test2.mjs and all library files into the artifact tree.
Serial performed local differential tests and delivered a final answer with a complete runnable structure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial still failed 20 official samples despite its extensive local checks; that residual quality gap is an ordinary implementation/evaluator mismatch rather than a parallel coordination pattern.
Parallel component modules may have had latent issues, but the official zero score is already explained by the missing entry file.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership existed: six library module groups were assigned and the parent also implemented argparse manually. The failure was not absence of an implementation owner.
The workflow explicitly planned an integration agent after child implementation; integration was blocked by the stalled child and incomplete takeover, not unassigned.
The workflow assigned entry-point and barrel assembly to the integration phase, so the required deliverable had an intended owner even though that phase never completed.
The parent workflow owned the end-to-end pipeline through implement, integrate, fuzz, review, and fix phases. Its failure was execution governance, not owner absence.
Parallel implementation began immediately in multiple module children; productive work was not blocked behind a single mandatory serial preflight gate.
Investigation and implementation overlapped: children wrote modules while the parent continued probing. The failure was not a separated investigation phase before implementation.
The indispensable path was blocked by the argparse child failure/takeover episode. Starvation is a downstream budget symptom of that same chain, not an independent allocation boundary.
The run used many child tokens, but the direct event was one repeatedly stalled required child and an incomplete takeover. There is no separate excessive-breadth episode to retain.
The argparse scope was difficult, but the more specific observed boundary is the parent-visible failed/stalled child that was not fully taken over before closure.
The workflow brief included the task, environment, acceptance, module layout, and delivery requirements. The child did not fail because a known requirement was omitted from its brief.
The workflow supplied a detailed exact interface contract for every module. No independently produced incompatible interface drove the final failure.
There is no evidence that a known requirement or finding was lost during transfer; the stalled child received the same broad project context and repeated work.
Child and workflow handoffs were large, but no receiver failed because a completed handoff was too bulky to reduce; the aggregate workflow never reached integration.
No actor is shown consuming a superseded workspace or requirement report; the material state at closure was an unfinished blocked workflow.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached a decision point and remained unadjudicated. The delivered problem was absence of final assembly.
Parallel made no observable whole-task completion decision: final.txt is empty, the workflow result is null, and the process timed out before completion.
The argparse retries did repeat similar probing, but that is the same stalled-child chain as the retained failure-propagation event and does not add an independent consequence.
